Split along the short axis to preserve the long bar gesture and open the frontage condition.
Create a substantial void that can operate as an entry seam/court instead of a token notch.
Keep the split open so the public ground relation is legible.
Add a courtyard macro to strengthen the required public void and respond to the access edge.
Keep the court sizable enough to read as usable public space.
Orient the open side to the verified access side so the frontage becomes active.

Open the mass along its short dimension to create a legible ground void toward the access side rather than a uniform sealed front.
Make the split large enough to register as public space and entry rather than a superficial crease.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent stepped bar in all four views, with good silhouette consistency and acceptable repair integrity, but it reads as a sealed, generic stacked mass with almost no public void or active threshold. The blue access edge is not answered by a visible court, notch, undercut, or entry seam, so the ground relation is semantically opposite to the neighborhood_living brief. The stepped profile has some precedent resonance and the dominant mass is legible, but the form still behaves like an object rather than a compact street building with an occupiable public edge. Because the program contract explicitly requires an active ground edge and one clear public void or terrace, the current mass cannot pass program fit.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied from the provided views, but the open-space logic does not respond coherently to the verified access edge.
The form is readable in all views, so failure is not due to incoherence; it is due to missing public threshold and weak program semantics.
The step silhouette is acceptable as a massing device, but here it does not produce a meaningful section or ground condition for neighborhood living.
